ran_primary.title: RAN: A randomness-anchored watermark attacking network with stealth and effectiveness
ran_primary.authors: Fan Li; Du Li; Kunqi Li; Yanyu Jiang; Yanlin Leng; Kai Zhou; Yong Tang
ran_primary.inspected_sections: Methods: architecture/losses, Equations 1--6; Experiments: datasets/training/metrics, Equations 7--11; Results and Discussion. Cached main text lines 78--163; all rows of separately cached official Tables 1--3.
ran_primary.mechanism: A 17-layer 54.4M-parameter U-Net learns to preserve input pixels while making the extracted watermark match uniform-random targets, using MSE or KL-divergence watermark loss. Training uses an extraction-dependent loss; lack of original payload knowledge is not proof of a decoder-free or universal black-box attack.
ran_primary.models: DWT(Haar, one level)-DCT(LL)-SVD watermark images; transfer evaluation on Watermark Anything Model (WAM) with 32-bit strings. No SD1.5, SDXL, diffusion model or independently trained diffusion autoencoder is evaluated.
ran_primary.strength_noise: Learned attack: alpha=1; beta=1e-6 for MSE or 1 for KLD. Uniform-random watermark targets; their exact numeric support NR. Comparators: average3x3, Gaussian5x5, median3x3, salt-pepper SNR=.95, Gaussian variance=.005, JPEG Q30/50/70.
ran_primary.sampler_steps: No diffusion sampler/timesteps: one feed-forward attack. Pretrain pixel MSE 50 epochs/batch40/lr1e-5, then30 epochs/batch30/Adam/lr1e-4; four-fold cross-validation model selection. No inference severity sweep reported.
ran_primary.prompt: Not applicable; natural cover images, no text conditioning or guidance.
ran_primary.resolution: 512x512 RGB covers; binarized32x32 CIFAR10 watermark images (1,024 pixels); additional32-bit WAM strings.
ran_primary.image_counts: 5,000 randomly selected ImageNet covers and5,000 CIFAR10 watermark images; 4,000 training/1,000 independent test covers. Table3 WAM uses the described testing evaluation, but a separate WAM-specific denominator and number of repetitions are NR; Table1 is one turtle image.
ran_primary.metrics: Mean(SD) SSIM/PSNR, watermark NC/BER; per-RGB-channel PSNR for one example. No calibrated FPR, image-level TPR/ASR, owner/payload verdict, LPIPS or uncertainty interval. SD is dispersion, not a confidence interval.
ran_primary.limits: Only two embedding schemes; traditional mean BER.240 does not establish random/chance decoding despite the randomness objective. WAM near-.5 mean BER is not calibrated image-level removal. Captions of Tables2--3 identify I_co versus I_a, while the metric definitions and narrative use I_w versus I_a: quality-reference conflict unresolved. Exact WAM checkpoint/native settings, random support/seeds, extractor-gradient handling and WAM-specific n are NR. No forensic stealth test; no F5 or independent-encoder transfer evidence; reported inference .022s on their setup is not a server cost estimate.
ran_primary.design_consequence: Include as a recent non-diffusion removal benchmark and an untested learned-attack limitation. Do not import BER as our endpoint or add an attack, baseline, proposal or compute cost to the frozen SDXL study.
